code: library(dplyr)  mpg %>% group_by(manufacturer) %>%   summarise(mean_cty = mean(cty)) %>%   bar_chart(     x = "manufacturer",     y = "mean_cty",     xFontSize = 10,     yFontSize = 10,     fill = "orange",     strokeWidth = 2,     ytitle = "average cty value",     title = "Average City Miles per Gallon by manufacturer"   ) mpg %>% group_by(manufacturer) %>%   summarise(mean_cty = mean(cty)) %>%   bar_chart(     x = "manufacturer",     y = "mean_cty",     sort = "ascending",     xFontSize = 10,     yFontSize = 10,     fill = "orange",     strokeWidth = 1,     ytitle = "average cty value",     title = "Average City Miles per Gallon by manufacturer",     titleFontSize = 16   )

text: dumbbell chart (also called connected dot plot) shows two values per category dots joined horizontal line. clearest way communicate gap change two groups, time points, conditions across many categories , grouped bar chart require much visual scanning reach conclusion. New York Times Economist use format regularly. chart works equally well comparing two conditions within time period. compare average city highway fuel economy across vehicle classes using mpg dataset:
code: life_exp <- data.frame(   country   = c("Brazil", "China", "Egypt", "India",                 "Japan", "Mexico", "Nigeria", "Turkey"),   year_1952 = c(50.9, 44.0, 41.9, 37.4, 63.0, 50.8, 36.3, 43.6),   year_2007 = c(72.4, 72.9, 71.3, 64.7, 82.6, 76.2, 46.9, 71.8) )  dumbbell_chart(   data     = life_exp,   x1       = "year_1952",   x2       = "year_2007",   y        = "country",   x1Label  = "1952",   x2Label  = "2007",   title    = "Life expectancy: 1952 vs 2007",   xtitle   = "Life expectancy (years)",   sort     = "ascending" ) library(dplyr)  mpg_summary <- mpg |>   group_by(class) |>   summarise(city = mean(cty), highway = mean(hwy))  dumbbell_chart(   data    = mpg_summary,   x1      = "city",   x2      = "highway",   y       = "class",   x1Label = "City",   x2Label = "Highway",   col1    = "steelblue",   col2    = "darkorange",   title   = "City vs highway fuel economy by class",   xtitle  = "Miles per gallon",   sort    = "ascending" )

text: slope chart (slopegraph) places two values per category two vertical axes, typically “” “” two different years, connects straight line. steepness direction line tell glance rose, fell, ranking changed. Edward Tufte popularised form Visual Display Quantitative Information (1983) chart government receipts across rich countries, New York Times graphics desk used regularly ever since. Use small--moderate number categories measured exactly two points; many categories many time points, line chart better choice. line labelled category name value ends, labels overlap nudged apart vertically. default lines colored direction (increase decrease). Hover line emphasise fade others. Use highlight tell story categories: rest drawn muted grey give context without competing attention. compare life expectancy 1952 2007 using gapminder dataset:
code: # Current receipts of government as a percentage of GDP, 1970 vs 1979 # (adapted from Edward Tufte's classic slopegraph) receipts <- data.frame(   country = c("Sweden", "Netherlands", "Norway", "Britain", "France",               "Germany", "Belgium", "Canada", "Finland", "Italy",               "United States", "Greece", "Switzerland", "Spain", "Japan"),   y1970 = c(46.9, 44.0, 43.5, 40.7, 39.0, 37.5, 35.2, 35.2, 34.9, 30.4,             30.3, 26.8, 26.5, 22.5, 20.7),   y1979 = c(57.4, 55.8, 52.2, 39.0, 43.4, 42.9, 43.2, 35.8, 38.2, 35.7,             32.5, 30.6, 33.2, 27.1, 26.6) )  slope_chart(   data       = receipts,   start      = "y1970",   end        = "y1979",   group      = "country",   startLabel = "1970",   endLabel   = "1979",   digits     = 1,   title      = "Government receipts as % of GDP",   height     = 520 ) library(gapminder) library(dplyr) library(tidyr)  countries <- c("China", "India", "Japan", "Brazil", "Nigeria",                "Egypt", "Germany", "United States", "South Africa")  life <- filter(gapminder, year %in% c(1952, 2007), country %in% countries) life <- select(life, country, year, lifeExp) life <- pivot_wider(life, names_from = year, values_from = lifeExp,                     names_prefix = "y")  slope_chart(   data       = life,   start      = "y1952",   end        = "y2007",   group      = "country",   startLabel = "1952",   endLabel   = "2007",   highlight  = c("China", "South Africa"),   digits     = 1,   title      = "Life expectancy: 1952 vs 2007" )

title: Time series and trends
text: lower upper draw confidence forecast ribbon around line. Holt-Winters forecast base R’s stats package: rollmean draws trailing moving average raw series, kept faint line (showRaw = FALSE hides ). Missing values leave gaps lines: options include yScale = "log", yZero, dateFormat, turning navigator, rangeButtons, zoom, legend, endLabels animate.
code: fit <- HoltWinters(log(AirPassengers)) fc <- predict(fit, n.ahead = 24, prediction.interval = TRUE)  passengers <- rbind(   data.frame(date = zoo::as.Date(time(AirPassengers)),              value = as.numeric(AirPassengers), lo = NA, hi = NA,              series = "Observed"),   data.frame(date = zoo::as.Date(time(fc)), value = exp(fc[, "fit"]),              lo = exp(fc[, "lwr"]), hi = exp(fc[, "upr"]),              series = "Forecast") )  line_chart(   passengers,   x = "date", y = "value", group = "series",   lower = "lo", upper = "hi",   colors = c(Observed = "#4269d0", Forecast = "#ff725c"),   events = c("Forecast starts" = as.Date("1961-01-01")),   valueFormat = ",.0f",   title = "Airline passengers: Holt-Winters forecast" ) set.seed(3) samples <- data.frame(   time = seq(as.POSIXct("2026-03-01 09:00", tz = "UTC"), by = "5 min", length.out = 400),   cpu  = 40 + cumsum(rnorm(400)),   mem  = 60 + cumsum(rnorm(400, 0, 0.5)) ) samples$cpu[150:170] <- NA # a monitoring outage  line_chart(   samples,   x = "time",   y = c("cpu", "mem"),   rollmean = 12,   hlines = c(SLA = 70),   valueSuffix = "%",   title = "Server load",   subtitle = "5-minute samples with a 1-hour moving average" )

text: streamgraph() inspired Highcharts streamgraph: stacked areas flowing around centred (wiggle) baseline, labels drawn inside layer, crosshair tooltip interactive legend. Unlike stacked_area_chart(), takes long data. Hover layer highlight , click legend item hide show . offset = "expand" turns stream 100% stacked view:
code: set.seed(2026) years  <- 1980:2020 genres <- c("Rock", "Pop", "Hip hop", "Electronic", "Country",             "R&B", "Jazz", "Metal", "Reggae", "Latin") peaks  <- c(1984, 1999, 2012, 2008, 1993, 2003, 1981, 1990, 1986, 2018) sizes  <- c(60, 55, 70, 40, 30, 35, 18, 25, 15, 45) music  <- expand.grid(year = years, genre = genres) idx    <- match(music$genre, genres) music$listeners <- round(   sizes[idx] * exp(-((music$year - peaks[idx]) / 9)^2) + runif(nrow(music), 1, 6) )  streamgraph(   data        = music,   x           = "year",   group       = "genre",   value       = "listeners",   valueFormat = ",.0f",   xtitle      = "Year",   title       = "Music genres, 1980-2020 (simulated listeners)" ) phones <- data.frame(   year   = rep(as.numeric(rownames(WorldPhones)), ncol(WorldPhones)),   region = factor(rep(colnames(WorldPhones), each = nrow(WorldPhones)),                   levels = colnames(WorldPhones)),   phones = as.vector(WorldPhones) )  streamgraph(phones, x = "year", group = "region", value = "phones",             offset = "expand", order = "descending", curve = "monotoneX",             colorPalette = "Set2", title = "Share of telephones by region")

title: Time series and trends
text: calendar_heatmap() inspired signature heatmap Frappe Charts GitHub’s contribution graph. draws one rounded square per day week--weekday grid, one panel per year, “Less … ” legend staggered fade-. Hover day see value, legend square highlight every day color bucket. Data spanning several years drawn one panel per year:
code: set.seed(2026) days <- seq(as.Date("2026-01-01"), as.Date("2026-12-31"), by = "day") weekday <- !(format(days, "%u") %in% c("6", "7")) activity <- data.frame(   day     = days,   commits = rpois(length(days), ifelse(weekday, 6, 1.5)) * rbinom(length(days), 1, 0.8) )  calendar_heatmap(activity, date = "day", value = "commits", title = "Commits in 2026") set.seed(1) days <- seq(as.Date("2021-01-01"), as.Date("2023-12-31"), by = "day") season <- 10 + 8 * sin(2 * pi * as.numeric(format(days, "%j")) / 365) rainfall <- data.frame(day = days, rain = pmax(0, rnorm(length(days), season, 6)))  calendar_heatmap(   rainfall, date = "day", value = "rain", weekStart = "monday",   colors = c("#9be9a8", "#40c463", "#30a14e", "#216e39"),   valueLabel = "mm of rain", valueFormat = ",.1f",   title = "Daily rainfall, 2021-2023" )
